solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carry piece of sound equipment suggestive of ritual?

parts.note: to tote something is to carry it
MIC is short for microphone

explanation.surface: Someone lugging a speaker or microphone about, as if it were a sacred object in a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: a totem is an emblem venerated in ritual, so anything totemic hints at such rites.
explanation.definitionFit: Totemic means relating to a totem, the clan emblem at the centre of tribal ceremony and worship.

clue.text: Ancient city grasping a way of buying up prize

indicators.note: a city grasping something holds it within its walls

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: HP is hire purchase, the British term for buying on instalments

explanation.surface: An old city clutching at a means of purchase to snap up a reward.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or other award given as a prize.

clue.text: A male beast without tail in strange art in flat

indicators.note: in puts the first pieces inside the anagram
strange means the word is made odd, its letters rearranged
without tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a bull is a male bovine beast

explanation.surface: A docked bull inside an odd artwork displayed in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns ART into TAR, and ABUL goes inside after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabular means shaped like a table, broad and flat, as of a rock formation.

clue.text: Cavity in heart needing attention

parts.note: the heart of a thing is its middle
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A hole in the heart that needs medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle ear is the air-filled chamber behind the eardrum, a cavity in the skull.

clue.text: Host briefly entertaining monster, a sort of accountant

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds it inside
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a compere is the host of a show
a troll is a monster of folklore

explanation.surface: A TV presenter has a beast on the show alongside a financial officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims COMPERE to COMPER; 'Host' is a show's presenter, not someone throwing a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A comptroller is a controller of finances, an official who audits accounts.

clue.text: Theatre food is tasted again

parts.note: REP is repertory theatre
EATS is informal for food

explanation.surface: At the theatre bar, the snack keeps coming back up after the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Food that 'repeats' on you is tasted again, as with indigestion.
explanation.definitionFit: When food repeats, its flavour returns in the mouth after eating, an idiomatic sense of the verb.

clue.text: Ladder lets one escape from dilapidated building

indicators.note: letting the numeral escape from the building takes it out

parts.note: a ruin is a dilapidated building
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A ladder lets someone climb out of a crumbling house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladder' is not for climbing: it is a run in tights or stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder in British usage is a run, a line of unravelled stitches in hosiery.

clue.text: Very good bed's embroidered decoration

parts.note: PI is short for pious, very good
a cot is a bed; the 's is read as has, a link

explanation.surface: A fine bedspread has stitched ornament on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small loop of thread forming an ornamental edging in lace or embroidery.

clue.text: A boy initially enthralled by east European entertainer

indicators.note: something enthralled by another is held captive inside it

parts.note: a Croat is from Croatia in eastern Europe

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter

explanation.surface: A lad captivated by a performer from eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat is a circus performer of gymnastic feats, one kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Try me out with my singular correspondence!

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual invitation to sample the speaker's one-of-a-kind letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' is not letters but matching of parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Symmetry is exact correspondence of parts on either side of a line or around a centre.

clue.text: Married chum's brought into Middle East location as investigator

indicators.note: something brought into a place ends up inside it, so these letters go within the country

parts.note: Oman is a country in the Middle East
a bud is a chum, so chum's gives BUD'S

explanation.surface: A married man's friend is posted to the Gulf to look into something.
explanation.walkthrough: MBUDS goes after the O of OMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official who investigates complaints against organisations.

clue.text: American cannon got from vehicle when given order

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An American gun is retrieved from a truck once the command is given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cannon' is not artillery: in billiards a cannon is a shot striking two balls, which Americans call a carom.
explanation.definitionFit: Carom is the American term for the billiards shot the British call a cannon.

clue.text: Room for keeping a type of food

indicators.note: a container for keeping something holds it within, so the room wraps the letter

parts.note: a hall is a room

explanation.surface: A pantry set aside for storing one particular kind of provision.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal food is prepared according to Islamic dietary law, so it names a category of food.

clue.text: Board behind reversing vehicle that can be easily dealt with

definitions.text: that can be easily dealt with

indicators.note: the board comes behind, after the reversed vehicle
a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so the word for it is read the other way

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
a table is a board, as in board and lodging or a flat surface

explanation.surface: A plank sits behind a backing van, a load that is easy to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractable means docile or manageable, readily handled or controlled.

clue.text: Insincerity of thank you drowned in sentiment

indicators.note: something drowned in a thing is submerged inside it

parts.note: affection is a tender sentiment
TA is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A thank-you smothered in gushing emotion rings false.
explanation.definitionFit: Affectation is artificial behaviour meant to impress, a pretence or insincerity.

clue.text: He'd get reform, if violently

indicators.note: violently signals these letters being thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: He would bring about change, if necessary by force.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a freedom fighter seeks reform through violence.
explanation.definitionFit: A freedom fighter takes up arms to overthrow an oppressive regime, pursuing change by force.

clue.text: Spooner's dry grass, territory that would do for dog

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: hay is dried grass
ground is territory

explanation.surface: A hayfield would suit a dog fine, as the old don might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of HAY GROUND gives GRAY HOUND, sounding like the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The greyhound is a slender breed of racing dog.

clue.text: Thief beats up beloved in Paris

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to tan is to beat, as in tan someone's hide
cher is French for dear or beloved

explanation.surface: A burglar roughs up a sweetheart in the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatcher grabs things and runs, a kind of thief.

clue.text: Nice clues composed with an art that will show intellectual discipline

indicators.note: letters composed are put together afresh, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Well-written crossword clues treated as an art form become a field of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural science, such as physics or biology, is a branch of learning, a scholarly discipline.

clue.text: RIP! Old females depart quickly

parts.note: to rip is to tear
F is female, doubled FF for females

explanation.surface: A gravestone inscription as old ladies hurry off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'RIP' looks like rest in peace but is just the verb rip.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear off is to rush away at speed.

clue.text: With river flooding in, send for solution to problem

indicators.note: the river flooding in pours inside the other word

parts.note: to call someone is to send for them
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: With the river bursting its banks, summon a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all is a panacea, a remedy for every difficulty.

clue.text: Guide soldiers over Dartmoor landmark?

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the soldiers above the landmark

parts.note: MEN are soldiers, the ranks
a tor is a rocky hilltop, typical of Dartmoor in Devon

explanation.surface: A leader takes troops across a famous outcrop on the moor.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is an adviser who guides a less experienced person.

clue.text: Restaurant offers excellent crumble, sweet course served retro-style

indicators.note: retro-style suggests going back, so the whole string is served written backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI
to rot is to crumble away
a tart is a sweet course, a dessert

explanation.surface: A menu offering a superb crumble and a dessert done in a retro way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumble' looks like a dessert beside 'sweet course' but is the verb, to rot. AIROTTART is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian eating place.

clue.text: The bird — he avoided dog

indicators.note: the word he is avoided, left out of the preceding word

parts.note: the rail is a marsh bird

explanation.surface: A man keeps clear of a hound and a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is the verb, to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to trail them, following persistently.

clue.text: Hack possibly putting run in stockings?

indicators.note: in places the run inside the stockings

parts.note: hose are stockings
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A careless pull putting a ladder in someone's tights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' is not a writer but a hired riding horse; 'possibly' says it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is an ordinary riding horse, so it is one example of the answer.

clue.text: Illicit drink about to be removed, leading to a kerfuffle

indicators.note: removed tells us the letter for about is taken away from the drink

parts.note: hooch is illicitly made liquor
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: Moonshine is about to be confiscated, leading to a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a fuss or commotion, a near synonym of kerfuffle.

clue.text: One drug-dealer, short worker at end of street offering cocaine?

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed at the end of the abbreviation for street

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: short tells us to drop the last letter

parts.note: a mule smuggles drugs for dealers
an ant is a worker in the insect colony

explanation.surface: A pusher on the street corner selling cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks cocaine as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocaine is a drug that excites the nervous system, one example of a stimulant.

clue.text: A daughter overlooked by son is out of sorts

indicators.note: in a down clue being overlooked by means sitting below, so son goes on top

explanation.surface: A girl ignored by her brother feels gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of sorts means low in spirits, unhappy.

clue.text: Maybe rabbit turned and ran, being disconcerted

indicators.note: turned means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: rabbit is an example of fur, game with fur as opposed to feather
fled means ran

explanation.surface: A startled rabbit wheeled and bolted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffled means flustered or upset, thrown off balance.

clue.text: Lunar domain — no sea, awfully lumpy

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so these letters are jumbled
no tells us the sea is left out of the word

parts.note: the main is the open sea

explanation.surface: The moon's surface, waterless, looks terribly bumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes MAIN out of DOMAIN to leave DO; LUNARDO is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodular means having nodules, small knots or lumps.
